variants.headline: Looking back: shipbuilding for the colony route
variants.sub: Shipbuilding by the home world has provided a larger vessel or another vessel for the colony route.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The home world had built a larger ship or an additional ship for the colony route.

A ship has been built for the route. Good material for a grand picture of the future; less useful as proof of what is on a shop shelf today. Keep the distinction clear. Building a vessel and watching it arrive are different stories, however attractive it is to combine them.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

The contribution of {target} should be assessed through the reported construction, without assuming an unreported improvement in service. This account establishes a vessel development, not the full terms of future voyages.

variants.headline: Looking back: route gains a shipbuilding development
variants.sub: The home world has built a larger ship or an additional ship for the colony route.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: A larger ship or one more ship had been built for the colony route.

A ship has been built for the route. Good material for a grand picture of the future; less useful as proof of what is on a shop shelf today. Keep the distinction clear. Building a vessel and watching it arrive are different stories, however attractive it is to combine them.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

The contribution of {target} should be assessed through the reported construction, without assuming an unreported improvement in service. This account establishes a vessel development, not the full terms of future voyages.
